A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same research, retaining the three vulnerability mechanisms and robotic prototype despite the BADROBOT retitling. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. The supplied v2 ends after its references without the mentioned appendix; v3 includes Appendices A-J.

before.justification: v2 reports original robotic demonstrations in Figures 1 and 5 and observed model interactions in Sections 4.2-4.3. These qualitative experimental outcomes qualify despite the absence of quantitative result tables.

after.justification: v3 reports original digital, simulation, physical-robot, and mitigation experiments in Sections 4-5, Tables 1-3, and the supplementary results.

M1.justification: The three attack procedures are retained: contextualized jailbreak prompts, structured-output enforcement, and GPT-4-assisted semantic rephrasing. v3 renames Jailbreak Exploit as Contextual Jailbreak and supplies pseudocode and exact prompts, without establishing a different attack algorithm. The semantic-consistency defense formula is also retained.

E1.justification: Beyond v2's prototype demonstrations, v3 evaluates RLBench object-interaction and spatial-composition tasks, VirtualHome household tasks, PyBullet tabletop scenarios, and VisProg image editing and object tagging (Section 4.3; Appendix F). These substantially extend task and environment coverage. The benchmark's seven harmful-action categories remain the same.

E2.justification: v3 reports a systematic comparison against Disguised Intent, Role Play, Structured Response, Virtual AI Simulation, and Hybrid Strategies, using 100 collected prompts and a Vanilla control (Tables 1/A1). v2 illustrates direct-query and role-play behavior and discusses structured responses, but does not report this expanded comparator suite.

E3.justification: v3 introduces quantitative protocols using manipulation success rate and GPT-4 harmfulness ratings, a five-model evaluation including LLaVA-1.5-7B, and 35 physical evaluations per attack. The retained benchmark's reported size changes from 230 to 277 queries. New simulation protocols are specified, although Code as Policies query counts conflict between Section 4.3 and Appendix F.3.

E4.justification: v2 discusses potential mitigations without reporting their effectiveness. v3 tests consistency validation and world-model fine-tuning on LLaVA (Table 3), analyzes failures of conventional jailbreak transfer (Appendix D.1), and quantifies the suffix/no-suffix contrast (Tables 2/A2). These add substantial controlled robustness and component analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 newly documents averaging results over three contextual-jailbreak prompts to reduce prompt-specific instability. This adds a limited aggregation practice, not evidence of increased independent repeated runs. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive quantitative findings absent from v2's qualitative demonstrations. Table 2 reports GPT-4-turbo MSRs of 0.83, 0.66, and 0.65 for the three attacks versus 0.25 Vanilla; Section 4.4 reports physical MSR of 68.57% versus 22.85%. Simulation results, harmfulness scores, and mitigation outcomes are also added. These are newly reported measurements, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2.2 adds an expected-safety maximization objective in Equation 1, beyond v2's universally quantified safety condition. Most remaining formalization changes preserve the existing binary safety logic or make prompt transformations explicit. Neither version supplies substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of physical-world vulnerability and three distinct risk mechanisms remain. v3 adds explicit comparative-superiority claims and foregrounds applicability to established frameworks and the benchmark as contributions. This refines the claimed contribution scope while retaining the original central scientific finding.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving conflicts with robotic system prompts, speech-recognition losses, jointly malicious outputs defeating consistency checks, and fine-tuning's uneven safety effects. Appendix F also qualifies ProgPrompt success as attempted execution despite incomplete tasks and acknowledges VisProg's differences from embodied systems. These materially extend v2's mechanism discussion and limitations.

D1.justification: v3 supplies exact attack and system prompts, action interfaces, the automated judging rubric, benchmark composition, prompt-collection procedures, server specifications, and expanded robot/camera details (Appendices B, E-J). Much of this was only referenced or briefly described in v2. However, v3 omits v2's direct project and benchmark-repository links; this changes access information without establishing that the resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 retains much of v2's general background in Appendix A but adds dedicated positioning against embodied-system adversarial robustness, discrimination, safety frameworks, and backdoor research (Section 6). Newly discussed works include Wu et al., Hundt et al., Azeem et al., SafeEmbodAI, and RiskAwareBench. Novelty is positioned more specifically around no-box malicious robotic manipulation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, terminology, and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten around BADROBOT. Risk analysis becomes a separate conceptual section; general background and policy material move to appendices; related work moves near the end; and conclusions and limitations are combined. This substantially reorganizes the retained material.

P2.justification: v3 adds comparison and mitigation tables, harmfulness radar charts, simulation plots, algorithm panels, benchmark graphics, and extensive simulation and UR3e demonstration grids. It also revises the pipeline graphic and attack illustrations and removes v2's separate linguistic-versus-action-space comparison diagram. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's principal evidentiary weakness: broad vulnerability claims supported mainly by demonstrations. Comparative evaluations, tests across external frameworks, quantified physical trials, and mitigation experiments provide substantially stronger support, while the appendices make procedures inspectable. Limitations remain: some Table A1 averages conflict with displayed category scores, Code as Policies query counts disagree, and direct artifact links disappear. These shortcomings temper confidence in exact estimates but do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and documentation.
